title: Awe
summary: Classic prototype account of awe (vastness + need for accommodation) and experimental evidence that awe increases prosociality and openness to transcendent frames via a “small self.”
summary_html: Classic prototype account of awe (vastness + need for accommodation) and experimental evidence that awe increases prosociality and openness to transcendent frames via a “small self.”
content_html:
Awe

Definition: Emotion elicited by vastness that challenges existing schemas.
Domains: Nature, art/music, spirituality/ritual, science/knowledge, leadership.
Immediate effects: Perceptual expansion, humble self-appraisal, curiosity.

Concept Chain

Awe → Small Self → Prosociality + Openness to Transcendence

Perceived vastness + need for accommodation (prototype model).
→
Reduced self-focus; increased connectedness.
→
Helping, generosity, sharing, ethical concern.
+
Greater receptivity to spiritual or “larger-than-self” interpretations.

Experiments: How does it change behaviour?

  • Inductions: videos of vast nature; standing under towering trees; narrative recall.
  • Outcomes: ↑ helping (e.g., picking up pens), ↑ generosity, ↓ entitlement, ↑ ethical decision-making.
  • Mediation: Effects often mediated by small self and connectedness.

Robustness & Boundary Conditions

  • Cross-context generality: Observed in lab, field, and quasi-naturalistic settings.
  • Varieties of awe: Threat-based awe may reduce prosociality vs. nonthreatening awe; appraisal patterns matter.
  • Duration: Effects are typically short-lived but can cumulate via repeated exposure (e.g., nature engagement, ritual).
  • Cultural lenses: Spiritual interpretations vary; openness to transcendence is moderated by prior beliefs and norms.

References

  • Anderson, C. L., Monroy, M., & Keltner, D. (2018). Awe in nature, prosociality, and well-being. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 115(2), 297–314.
  • Keltner, D., & Haidt, J. (2003). Approaching awe, a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion. Cognition and Emotion, 17(2), 297–314.
  • Piff, P. K., Dietze, P., Feinberg, M., Stancato, D. M., & Keltner, D. (2015). Awe, the small self, and prosocial behavior. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 108(6), 883–899.
  • Preston, J. L., Wegner, D. M., & others. (2013). Awe, humility, and spirituality. Psychology of Religion and Spirituality, 5(3), 200–210.
  • Stellar, J. E., Gordon, A. M., Piff, P. K., Cordaro, D., Anderson, C., Bai, Y., Maruskin, L. A., & Keltner, D. (2017). Self-transcendent emotions and their social functions. Emotion Review, 9(3), 255–270.
